adversarialReviewOfThePilot: The law test could have been vacuous. `assert.match(source, /Omit<AnchorBase,\s*"children">/)` passes on a file that merely CONTAINS that string, so a component that took the Omit and then spread an untyped bag would still pass it. That is why the same test also renders ModelCite and asserts byte-for-byte output equality, and why the consumer suite watches the compiler actually reject a body. A prove:gates case that removes the Omit and watches the law test fire is being added with the remaining families, so the gate is not trusted on a passing run alone.

The `from` field would have been the easiest place to fabricate. There is no test on it, it is free text, and every existing entry names a product screen. Naming one here would have looked identical to the other 73 entries and been false.

`corpus: string` rather than `React.ReactNode` was a late correction. ReactNode would have re-opened the leak the Omit closes: ...section body...} /> renders body copy inside a component with no body slot, and every gate in this repo would be green on it.
